findings.excerpt:
theorem primeDigits_first {p : ℕ} [NeZero p] (u : ℕ) :
    (primeDigits p (u : ZMod (p^2))).1 = (u : ZMod p)
findings.problem: This is the canonical normalisation lemma for the first digit of a natural-number cast. It rewrites the compound term `(primeDigits p ↑u).1` to the simpler `(↑u : ZMod p)`. It cannot loop, because the RHS contains no `primeDigits`. Its only side condition is the instance `NeZero p`, which is found by instance synthesis. It is not tagged `@[simp]`, though, and `primeDigits` is an opaque `noncomputable def` with no simp lemmas. So `simp` cannot reduce the first digit of a cast. Callers must name the lemma by hand. PrimeDigitAverages.lean passes it to `simp only`, ActualArithmeticFluctuation.lean applies it with `exact`, and ArithmeticCoefficientProbability.lean passes it to `funext`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]`. Then `simp` can normalise `(primeDigits p (u : ZMod (p^2))).1` to `(u : ZMod p)`. The `simp only [..., primeDigits_first, ...]` call in `residuePrimePatterns_arithmetic` can then become a plain `simp` call, or keep its explicit lemma list. The statement and orientation stay unchanged. No companion lemma is needed, because the second digit has no comparable closed form.
findings.benefit: Goals that mention the first digit of an arithmetic residue reduce automatically to the plain cast. Each such goal currently needs an explicit rewrite with `primeDigits_first`. This also gives the three downstream call sites one canonical normal form, `(u : ZMod p)`.
